issue: Desktop SHA256 never verified: IDesktopInstaller adapter sets FullChecksumUrl=null, so DownloadAndStageAsync skips the hash gate at line 251; AssetSha256 fetched in CheckAsync is silently discarded — violates IUpdateSource.cs:60 security contract
fix: In the IDesktopInstaller.DownloadAndStageAsync adapter, either (a) pass info.AssetSha256 into the legacy UpdateInfo (add an ExpectedSha256 field checked alongside checksumUrl), or (b) verify the hash inline after DownloadAndStageAsync returns, before returning the extracted path.

issue: Trampoline repair uses powershell -Command with inline IWR+exec bootstrap — the exact AMSI heuristic shape (Trojan:Win32/ClickFix.DCW!MTB) that SelfRepair.cs:123 was fixed to avoid in v2.31.10-r2 by switching to -File with a temp .ps1
fix: Mirror SelfRepair.cs: write the bootstrap to a temp .ps1 via os.WriteFile, then invoke powershell.exe -File <path> instead of -Command <inline>.

issue: No desktop SHA-mismatch test: SideloadSource_DownloadAsync_ShaMismatch is pinned but there is no equivalent for the GitHubReleaseSource→UpdateChecker desktop path, concealing the UpdateChecker.cs:119 null-checksum gap
fix: Add a GitHubReleaseSource_DownloadAsync_ShaMismatch_Throws test that supplies a non-null AssetSha256, serves mismatched bytes via FakeHttpClient, and asserts InvalidOperationException with 'checksum mismatch'.
